verdict.rationale: Deepgram documents API-based creation of persisted agent configurations (UUID returned via the Console API), and the dg CLI ships a built-in MCP server for AI coding tools, so the agent-creation step can be done programmatically. However, the phone side relies on Twilio: Twilio streams audio to your server, which bridges it to the Voice Agent WebSocket, and nothing shows Deepgram itself attaching a number or placing a call. Missing for 10: first-party API/CLI/MCP number provisioning and attachment, a documented programmatic outbound-call trigger, evidence that the CLI/MCP covers voice agent provisioning, and hands-on corroboration of an end-to-end dashboard-free flow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can provision a complete voice agent end to end — create the agent, attach a number, and place a call — through the API, CLI, or MCP without touching the dashboard

citations.quote: Reusable Agent Configurations allow you to define and persist the agent block of your Settings message using the Deepgram API. Once created, you receive a UUID that can be passed in place of the full agent object
The dg CLI includes a built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that gives AI coding tools direct access to Deepgram APIs.
Telephony: connect voice agents to phone networks for inbound and outbound calls.
